title: Intestinal triacylglycerol synthesis in fat absorption and systemic energy metabolism
authors: Yen CE, Nelson DW, Yen MI
funder: This work was funded by the National Institutes of Health Grant DK088210 and US Department of Agriculture Grant WIS01442.
result: Narrative review. Triacylglycerol forms the bulk of animal fats and plant oils and accounts for approximately 95% of dietary fat. Pancreatic lipase prefers sn-1 and sn-3 ester bonds and yields fatty acids and sn-2 monoacylglycerol. In enterocytes the monoacylglycerol pathway, with MGAT2 and DGAT1 in the endoplasmic reticulum, accounts for more than 75% of postprandial intestinal triacylglycerol synthesis; DGAT1 is the only DGAT detected in human intestine. Triacylglycerol forms the core of ApoB-containing chylomicrons, whose assembly requires MTP.
